analysis:
Docs-only change to docs/provider/cli-reference.md (no code, config or protocol changes). Changed head ranges 956-962 and 1028-1043 are in unit :10; unit :11 has no changed lines and was reviewed as context.

1. Drain/stop text (lines 956-962): with the coordinator connection down, a drain with no unfinished work waits up to 10 s and finishes without acknowledgement. It says the disconnect already cancelled accepted work and nothing queued can still reach the coordinator. It also documents a 15 s per-model unload wait, after which a stuck native retirement is left to process exit. This describes behavior only and weakens no stated control. Relevant threat IDs are T-010 (cancellation propagation), T-028 (residual GPU data) and T-029 (availability). The doc assumes the claim is true: a disconnect cancels in-flight inference, and an unload that times out leaves decrypted data in memory only until the process exits. A later review should check ProviderLoop.unloadAllModelsForShutdown and ServiceDrain against this claim. I could not verify the code from the supplied evidence.

2. Status text (lines 1028-1043): this adds diagnostics that report enabled_models drift and models served outside the filter. It exposes the owner's own configuration through local CLI output and daemon-state fields (enabled_models_at_start, enabled_models_at_last_switch). It is not a new exposure boundary, since the file is local and owned by the operator. The docs state that model names and exact load figures stay out of the public logs. This is consistent with the privacy posture in T-058.

3. Other lines (Autopilot consent, logout, App Attest unenroll, the fan helper, prefix-cache posture) are unchanged context and match the canonical model: TB-011/T-053, TB-010, T-041, A-008. I found no contradiction with the threat model and no new attack surface. The T-041 prefix-cache description mentions no changed TTL or storage policy.

Residual question for integration: confirm the code matches the documented drain/unload semantics. This is a documentation-accuracy matter, not a vulnerability.
